scope.coverage: Every supplied cited-or-required record was investigated with directly read official registries/publisher/project sources. Unavailable exact identities remain explicitly unverified.
scope.exclusions: Three uncited/non-required bibliography records are outside this 92-record handoff. This bibliographic receipt does not certify empirical downloads or runtime checks; separate acquisition and validation receipts record those observations.

verdict: Bibliographic identities and specific topic mismatches were inspected; this is not blanket claim verification or biological validation.
evidence_discipline: Search used only for discovery. Metadata observations originate in Crossref/DataCite publisher deposits, official publisher pages, project registries or responsible institutions.
Registry identity, deposited abstract scope, manuscript inference, empirical parsing and biological validation are separate evidence levels.
Retrieval/parser failures are unavailable evidence, not invalid-source or fabrication findings.
Exact original unconfirmed article records and search candidates remain preserved below even when citation support was removed.
No second independent origin is implied merely by DOI resolver plus registry metadata; most records remain single-origin bibliographic evidence.
weakest_evidence_link: Exact primary metadata for retained Seeley1989 remains unavailable behind publisher/client challenges. Free1987 now has an ISBN-specific publisher identity. Two other exact article identities were unconfirmed and removed; the new project manuscript publication identity is not independently established.
next_discriminating_evidence: Obtain an inspectable exact Seeley1989 source and original documents if removed Johnson/Wcislo identities are to be restored. Claim-level causal/calibration assertions require study-level primary methods/results, not merely registry metadata.
credible_alternatives: Unidentified records may be miscited titles or incomplete author publication coverage rather than nonexistent works.
Differences between online publication year and issue year do not by themselves establish erroneous dating.
